entry.dc:title: Risk assessment in reserve estimation and open-pit planning
entry.dc:creator: Dowd P.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions Institution of Mining Metallurgy Section A
entry.dc:description: The effects of the uncertainty of the ore reserve on feasibility studies and open-pit mine design for a small gold-mining venture are explored. Geostatistical simulation is employed as a method of quantifying the risk associated with the use of grades and tonnages that have been estimated from sparse data. -Author

entry.dc:title: Mitigation of adverse effects at the Lezama-Leguizamon abandoned open-pit mine (Bilbao, northern Spain)
entry.dc:creator: Saiz de Omeñaca J.
entry.prism:publicationName: Environmental Geology
entry.dc:description: Solid fills arranged in 1-m-thick layers were prepared with stone blocks and pebbles of a drainage bed every 8 m. Runoff gathering in a well and the use of silts and mud lands for bordering and sealing the limestones are the main techniques employed for minimizing unfavorable effects at the Lezama-Leguizamon abandoned open-pit mine. Since there were waste disposal problems in the area, the rate of disposal has made the activity profitable. No significant faults have been detected by control studies, and the objectives are being achieved without problems. © 1993 Springer-Verlag.
entry.authkeywords: Limestone sealing | Mine reclamation | This abandoned open-pit mine

entry.dc:title: Computer-based optimization of open-pit mining sequences
entry.dc:creator: Huang S.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions of the Institution of Mining and Metallurgy Section A Mining Technology
entry.dc:description: An interactive model and corresponding computer software for optimization of the open-pit mining sequence have been developed at the Institute of Mining Engineering, Technical University of Berlin. The model is supported by graphics software and consists of three linear programming systems and a simulation module. With this model an optimum mining sequence for a multi-level open-pit mine can be determined under a criterion selected by the planner.

entry.dc:title: Evaluation of geological and geotechnical data by using GIS for the diggability classification of an open-pit mine
entry.dc:creator: Ayday C.
entry.prism:publicationName: Exploration Environment and Engineering Proc Ninth Thematic Conference on Geologic Remote Sensing Pasadena 1993 2 Vols
entry.dc:description: In many excavation projects careful consideration should be given to numerous factors including geological and topographic information, proximity of the excavation operation to waste disposal areas and environmental restrictions together with equipment characteristics. For the rapid achievement of this aim, adequate techniques of evaluating such complicated data is of prime importance. In an attempt to demonstrate such an application, this paper gives the use of Geographic Information Systems in conjunction with two selected diggability classification systems for the rippability assessment of a particular site. The approach described will be actually applicable to the selection of excavating equipment for a wide range of other mining and civil engineering projects. -Authors

entry.dc:title: Quick deals and raw deals: A perspective on abuses of public ADR principles in Texas resource conflicts
entry.dc:creator: Kartez J.
entry.prism:publicationName: Environmental Impact Assessment Review
entry.dc:description: Comparing the recent Texas Copper Company smelter controversy with the celebrated Homestake open-pit mine case a decade ago illustrates that opportunities exist for resolving difficult siting and resource development conflicts, but that such opportunities can be misused, and sound dispute resolution principles abused. The route to failed siting efforts is to ignore the established evidence of the need for processes that acknowledge all stakeholders and the need for treating environmental analysis as a joint effort among parties instead of as a battle over facts. Unfortunately, cases continue to exist where a narrow focus on the settlement, however creative it may be, is leading to failure because of contempt for or ignorance of the importance of pre-negotiation and in-negotiation process requirements. In short, the "quick deal" may be no bettern than "no deal" in environmental conflicts. © 1993.

entry.dc:title: A critical appraisal of the Whittle 3-D open-pit mine optimization software package
entry.dc:creator: Costelloe D.
entry.prism:publicationName: Geological Society Special Publication
entry.dc:description: In 1965 Lerch & Grossman produced a paper describing a 3-D algorithm based on graph theory which could be specifically applied to the optimization of open-pit mine designs. At the time, most computers were incapable of performing the large quantities of iterative calculations required by the method. A 2-D algorithm was also described which, though effective on sections, lost its optimized quality when sections were combined. The 3-D algorithm therefore remained the preferred option. In 1986 the Whittle 3-D open-pit optimization package was launched by Whittle Programming Ltd. This package utilized the Lerch-Grossman algorithm for the first time in a commercial software application. Since then the package has undergone a number of changes and improvements. The purpose of an optimization package is to produce the most cost effective and most profitable open-pit design from a block model of an orebody. It must be capable of rapidly analysing alternatives accurately; it must be able to carry out sensitivity analyses of different components to assess financial risk; it must allow frequent updates to take into account changes in costs etc. and it must allow the production of interim designs. In today's mining world, a hastily produced or non-rigorous design is financially unacceptable as the design determines the potential for profit or loss. To develop this further it is essential not just to make a profit but to maximize the return on investment. This paper appraises the ability of the Whittle 3-D package to satisfy this objective. © The Geological Society 1992.

entry.dc:title: GPR measurements for locating underground mine workings at an active open-pit mine
entry.dc:creator: Daniels J.J.
entry.prism:publicationName: Special Paper Geological Survey of Finland
entry.dc:description: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) measurements have been used recently at the Zortman Gold Mine (located in Zortman, Montana, USA) to locate underground mine workings beneath the current working level of the Zortman Open Pit Gold Mine. The igneous host rock is generally uniform, and GPR is routinely used to detect drifts, stopes, winzes and rooms located at depths of over 30 feet below the surface of the pit floor. The usefulness of GPR for detecting underground hazards is confirmed by blast hole drilling, with additional confirmation from historical underground maps of the old workings. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: Albitites and oligoclasite from Szklary (Lower Silesia)
entry.dc:creator: Muszynski M.
entry.prism:publicationName: Bulletin Polish Academy of Sciences Earth Sciences
entry.dc:description: Fine-crystalline leucocratic rocks, found within the serpentinite massif of Szklary (Lower Silesia) in the abandoned nickel open-pit mine, were studied by microscopic, X-ray, infrared adsorption spectroscopic and chemical methods. It has been concluded that they represent almost monomineral feldspathic rocks - albitites and oligoclasite. Results obtained, particularly REE contents indicate a genetic link between these rocks and lower-Silesian gabbros. -Authors

entry.dc:title: Hydrothermal and supergene uranium mineralization at the Osamu Utsumi mine, Poços de Caldas, Minas Gerais, Brazil
entry.dc:creator: Waber N.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Geochemical Exploration
entry.dc:description: The Osamu Utsumi uranium deposit in the Mesozoic alkaline complex of Poços de Caldas (MG, Brazil) is a product of subsequent hydrothermal and supergene processes. The lithology of the open-pit mine is composed of a sequence of volcanic and subvolcanic phonolites and nepheline syenite intrusions similar to those of the alkaline complex; volcanic breccia pipes of about 80 m in diameter also occur, characterized by UThZr-REE mineralization concentrated in the matrix. A strong hydrothermalism, related to the formation of the breccias, has resulted in the potassic alteration and pyritization of the phonolites and syenites, with a low-grade mineralization of disseminated pitch-blende. The potassic alteration has transformed all feldspars into pure potash feldspars, nepheline into illite and kaolinite, and clinopyroxenes, which are the primary REE-bearers, into mixtures of TiO<inf>2</inf>-rich minerals, clay minerals and pyrite. The enrichment of K, S, U, Th, Pb, Rb, Ba and Mo was accompanied by a strong depletion in Ca, Na, Mg and Sr. The fluid inclusion data indicate temperatures around 250°C and a KClH<inf>2</inf>O mixture with approximately 7 wt.% KCl for the hydrothermal fluids. For fluids in the breccia pipes that transported additional Zr, Hf, F and minor REEs, the inclusions indicate boiling and give temperatures of 210°C with 40-45 wt.% KCl for a KClNaClH<inf>2</inf>O brine containing FeSO<inf>4</inf> and KF. Uraninite, pitchblende and brannerite are the main U-carriers, and monazite the major REE-bearing mineral in the high-grade mineralization of the breccias. Ultramafic dykes (dated to 76 Ma) with carbonatitic affiliation put a younger age limit to the hydrothermal event. As a result of supergene weathering below a lateritic soil cover 20 to 40 m thick and a saprolite zone 15 to 60 m thick, the pyrites in the rocks have been oxidized to varying depths of 80 to 140 m below surface, resulting in a redox front marked by a contrasting color change from oxidized (reddish-brown) to reduced (bluish-grey). In the vicinity of water-bearing fissures these redox fronts have penetrated to greater depth. Due to mobilization in the oxidized zone and precipitation immediately below the redox front, a secondary mineralization of pitchblende, partly occurring as nodules associated with secondary pyrite, has been developed. This secondary pyrite is sometimes related with CdS, and has a δS of -13% compared to δS values of -3.63 to +1.24% for hydrothermal pyrites: the low δS values of the former are attributed to bacterial action. In the immediate vicinity of the redox front, dissolution of the potash feldspar becomes apparent and the kaolinite content begins to increase. The marked color change at the redox front is caused by the presence of hydrous ferric oxides that, with time, evolve from amorphous Fe-hydroxides to goethite and hematite. On the oxidized side alunite-jarosite minerals are frequent. The porosity increases by 5 to 8% (almost doubled) at the redox front. Gibbsite is present when potash feldspar has been removed at the saprolite-laterite contact. Uranium is partly retained in the oxidized zone by adsorption onto poorly crystalline phases and due to incorporation into hydrothermal refractory minerals. Many of the REEs are associated with clay-sized phosphates (including crandallite group minerals) and seem to be hardly mobilized by the oxidizing weathering fluids. Only a slight general loss of REEs was observed between oxidized and reduced rock, with the degree of loss being greater for the light REEs. Certain indications for a fractionation of Ce and Eu from the other REEs are present. © 1992.

entry.dc:title: An evaluation of the toxic gas pollution in an open-pit mine
entry.dc:creator: Panev T.
entry.prism:publicationName: Problemi Na Khigienata
entry.dc:description: The present work aims at giving a complete characteristic of the toxic chemical factor in the working environment of a pit "Kremikovtsi", for evaluating the occupational risk for the engaged workers. The basic pollution sources of the pit are the eliminating toxic gases during work from different types of machines and heavy-freight vans. The already measured concentrations of carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, nitric oxides, hydrocarbons, aldehydes and lead, manganese, ferrous and mercury aerosols in all working places of the pit are under MAC. The calculated total index of toxicity for all working places surpasses up to 3 times the unit and is rated. 1st degree--unfavourable conditions of work concerning the toxic chemical factor.

entry.dc:title: Grasberg open-pit. Ertsberg's big brother comes onstream in Indonesia
entry.dc:creator: Hickson R.
entry.prism:publicationName: Mining Engineering
entry.dc:description: The Grasberg copper-gold deposit was discovered in the spring of 1988, one year before the planned closure of Freeport Indonesia's original Ertsberg open-pit copper mine. In spite of Grasberg's remote location, 600 m (1968 ft) above the Ertsberg, atop a hitherto inaccessible mountain, Freeport-McMoRan brought its latest open-pit mine into production in the last week of 1989, less than two years after discovery. Freeport Indonesia's (FI) copper-gold mining operations are located in Irian Jaya, the easternmost province of Indonesia on the western side of the island of New Guinea.

entry.dc:title: Labour conditions and morbidity with temporary disability in the excavator operators engaged in the Karaganda open coal mines
entry.dc:creator: Lutsenko L.
entry.prism:publicationName: Meditsina Truda I Promyshlennaya Ekologiya
entry.dc:description: Studies performed at an open-pit mine in the Karaganda Region showed that excavator operators were exposed to the complex action of vibration, noise, unfavourable microclimate and dust in the parameters axceeding the existing norms. A comparative analysis of the levels of morbidity with temporary disability and the actual occupational conditions proved the latters' influence on the morbidity rate, particularly in case with diseases caused by respiratory infections, spinal disorders (radiculitis, lumbago), blood circulation disfunctions, all of which should be attributed to occupationally conditioned ailments. Hygienic and preventive measures, with due account of specific groups of diseases, can considerably improve the workers' health status and decrease morbidity with temporary disability rates.

entry.dc:title: Thermal decomposition and formation of properties of fine-grained coke from brown coals
entry.dc:creator: Unterberger O.
entry.prism:publicationName: Coke Chemistry USSR English Translation of Koks I Khimiya
entry.dc:description: Studies were conducted on a laboratory unit that stimulates heating of coal in a fluidized bed by heating the boosting bed of coal through the wall of a rotating retort. The installation permits running of the process over a wide range of rates of temperature rise right up to heat shock, as well as isothermal holding of the coal at the final coking temperature. Brown coal from the Irsha-Borodino open-pit mine of the Kansk-Achinsk Basin ground to a size of 83.4% content of <3 mm class was used for the study. Investigation of the possible rates of coking showed that the maximum rate of heating of the boosting coal particles is achieved during heat shock and amounts to 100-120°C/min. The conditions of heat shock most fully correspond to the conditions of heating of coal with a solid heat transfer agent during thermocontact coking, for which reason the rate of coking of 100-120°C/min was chosen to investigate the principles of pyrolysis of brown coal.

entry.dc:title: Performance monitoring of electric mining shovels
entry.dc:creator: Hendricks C.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions of the Institution of Mining and Metallurgy Section A Mining Technology
entry.dc:description: A review is presented of studies undertaken in a large open-pit mine with the aim of defining the relationship between shovel performance and muckpile characteristics, as governed by bench geology and ground preparation. The studies included the development and application of microprocessor-based instrumentation to monitor the performance of rotary blasthole drills and electric shovels. Particular attention is given to the methodology for the evaluation of shovel digging performance. Sample shovel performance data and their interpretation are presented to illustrate how this has been related to muckpile diggability in a range of digging conditions. A diggability index, based on hoist motor response, has been determined. Elements of dipper trajectory have also been considered in the interpretation of monitored motor responses.

entry.dc:title: On the problem of fuzzy searching for hard workability rocks in open-pit mine exploitation
entry.dc:creator: Kacewicz M.
entry.prism:publicationName: Mathematical Geology
entry.dc:description: The problem of fuzzy searching for hard workability rock areas is divided into two steps. The first is description of uncertainty of compressive strength, internal friction angle, and cohesion. The second is description of workability coefficient via fuzzy sets. The method presented is used in a computer program, which is an element of data base utility library. © 1989 International Association for Mathematical Geology.

entry.dc:title: Short term mine planning at Syncrude
entry.dc:creator: Malhotra Y.P.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: The synthetic crude oil from the oil sands with a consistently upward trend in production each year. The open-pit mine currently delivers an average of 300,000 tonnes of oil sands per day to the Extraction Plant. For the mining of oil sands, the mine is equipped with four draglines, four bucketwheel reclaimer/ conveyor systems and an auxiliary production system to supplement major equipment production. Overburden is stripped by a large fleet of shovels and trucks. All these systems combined will handle approximately 325 million tonnes of material in 1988. The effective technical support is crucial to the achievement of high production objectives. The short term mine planning functions to achieve these objectives, are performed by two groups; Overburden Engineering and Short Range Planning. The short term plans range from day to day operating plans to one year mine plans. This paper will discuss the short term planning process, the complexities and some of the challenges faced by the mine planning engineers. © 1989, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Development of a route determination system on open-pit mining using personal computer
entry.dc:creator: Hagiwara Y.
entry.prism:publicationName: Waseda Daigaku Rikogaku Kenkyusho Hokoku Bulletin of Science and Engineering Research Laboratory Waseda University
entry.dc:description: The authors have developed a haul road determination system for shovel and dump truck method hauling on open-pit mining sites. Under this system, the optimum haul road (or route) should provide the highest possible safety to the travelling dump truck as well as the shortest possible cycle time. Uncertain conditions and indefinite factors inherent to designing an open-pit mine have been simplified in order to put a personal computer into practical use. A simulation test has revealed that the use of this system has practical value up to 80 × 80 mesh data by translating BASIC to ASSEMBLER language.

entry.dc:title: Electrical equipment for heavy duty conveyors in open-pit mines
entry.dc:creator: Hartlief F.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The area to the west of Cologne as far as the borders with Belgium and the Netherlands contains the largest coherent deposit of lignite in the Federal Republic of Germany, covering approximately 2500 km<sup>2</sup>. 110×10<sup>6</sup> tonnes of lignite are produced annually in 4 open-pit mines using bucket-wheel excavators, conveyors, stockpile machines and spreaders; this requires transporting 450×10<sup>6</sup> m<sup>3</sup> of overburden each year. Consequently, the mass transport of coal and overburden, as 40% of the cost of an open-pit mine, is a major consideration within the context of engineering, economics and organization. The article describes the conveyors and their electrical systems.

entry.dc:title: Relationship between soil organic carbon and microbial biomass on chronosequences of reclamation sites
entry.dc:creator: Insam H.
entry.prism:publicationName: Microbial Ecology
entry.dc:description: The interrelationship between soil microorganisms and soil organic carbon was studied on an agricultural and on a forest chronosequence of open-pit mine reclamation soils. Thirty years after reclamation, soil carbon levels of 0.8% on the agricultural sites and 1.7% on the forest sites (A-horizon) were reached. Microbial biomass rose very fast to levels characteristic of undisturbed soils. Microbial carbon (C<inf>mier</inf>) was 57 mg·100 g<sup>-1</sup> soil after 15 years on the agricultural sites and 43 mg·100 g<sup>-1</sup> on the forest sites. The contribution of C<inf>mier</inf> to the total organic carbon (C<inf>org</inf>) decreased with time, more rapidly on the forest sites than on the agricultural ones. From the C<inf>mier</inf>r/C<inf>org</inf> ratio it became evident that both chronosequences had not yet reached a steady state within the 50 years of reclamation. A significant decrease of the metabolic quotient qCO<inf>2</inf> (microbial respiration per unit biomass) with time was observed on the agricultural sites but not on the forest sites. The C<inf>mier</inf>/C<inf>org</inf> ratio proved to be a reliable soil microbial parameter for describing changes in man-made ecosystems. For evaluating reclamation efforts, the C<inf>mier</inf>/C<inf>org</inf> ratio can be considered superior to its single components (C<inf>mier</inf> or C<inf>org</inf>) and to other parameters. © 1988 Springer-Verlag New York Inc.

entry.dc:title: Overview of hydraulic construction techniques utilized at the syncrude Canada Limited tailings pond.
entry.dc:creator: Yano L.
entry.prism:publicationName: In Hydraulic Fill Structures Speciality Conf Fort Collins U S A Aug 15 18 1988 D J A Van Zykl S G Vick Eds
entry.dc:description: The use of tailings sand from a tar-sand and open-pit mine in Alberta, Canada, to construct the containment dyke for the tailings pond is described by the foundation geology and the in-situ density of the compacted tailings sand. Construction techniques and the history of the tailings pond are outlined.

entry.dc:title: Phytogeochemical surveys within kimberlite bodies
entry.dc:creator: Komogorova L.
entry.prism:publicationName: Doklady Earth Science Sections
entry.dc:description: Based on certain theoretical assumptions, the authors conducted surveys within the Daldyn kimberlite field, Daldyn-Alakit district, Yakutia, in the Udachnaya, the Dal'nyaya and the Zarnitsa pipes. A survey was conducted along the south side of an open-pit mine and along separate profiles, where the authors sampled needles and small twigs of larches (Larix daurica) of roughly the same age. Elements characteristic of the kimberlite-dispersion halo (Ti, Ni, Cr and Fe) were detected in relatively high concentrations in the halo zone around the open-pit mine. The results of phytogeochemical sampling in the vicinity of the Zarnitsa pipe also confirm the possibility of using the phytogeochemical method to outline kimberlite pipes.

entry.dc:title: Quaternary stratigraphy and geochemistry at the Owl Creek Gold Mine, Timmins, Ontario, Canada
entry.dc:creator: Bird D.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Geochemical Exploration
entry.dc:description: The Owl Creek Gold Mine is located in Hoyle Township, approximately 18 km northeast of Timmins, Ontario, Canada. The open-pit mine exposes a sequence of altered and mineralized mafic tholeiitic volcanics bounded to the north and south by greywacke and argillite. Gold occurs in the free state in quartz veins, often with graphite, and as fine gold on surfaces of, and within fractures in, pyrite. The study was designed to determine the distribution and distance of transport of Au in overburden down-ice from subcropping Au mineralization. This required an understanding of the glacial history of the area. The Quaternary stratigraphy at Owl Creek was studied and sampled by means of 17 sonic and 15 reverse-circulation overburden drill holes near the open pit, and several overburden exposures in the open-pit walls. Nonmagnetic heavy-mineral concentrates (specific gravity >3.3) were made from the <2000 μm (-10 mesh) fraction of all overburden samples from the drill hole and section sampling. The heavy-mineral concentrates were analyzed for Au by neutron activation. A till pebble lithology study was done on the >2000 μm (-10 mesh) fraction of the sonic drill core. Our stratigraphic studies indicate that there were three major Wisconsinan (Weichselian) ice advances and one minor, late readvance in the Timmins area. The transport and deposition of sediments comprising the "Oldest", "Older", Matheson and Cochrane stratigraphic "packages" (oldest to youngest) are related to three ice advances and one readvance which moved towards 240° ± 10°, 150° ± 5°, 170° ± 5° and 130° ± 5°, respectively. Geochemically anomalous levels of Au in the overburden define two dispersal trains down-ice of the Owl Creek Gold Mine. One, in the "Older" lodgement till, is 400-500 m long. The other in Matheson ablation and waterlain tills, is approximately 700 m long. The till pebble lithology study showed that pebble counting can be used to approximate bedrock contacts, but may not necessarily identify the source rock type of the matrix. © 1987.

entry.dc:title: SETTLEMENT INSTRUMENTATION TO OBSERVE OPEN-PIT MINE BACKFILL AND A PROTOTYPE FOUNDATION IN WESTERN CANADA.
entry.dc:creator: Thomson S.
entry.prism:publicationName: Canadian Geotechnical Journal
entry.dc:description: The settlement of the spoil from one open-pit mining operation west of Edmonton, Alberta, was monitored by a series of magnetic extensometers installed in boreholes. Time-settlement plots indicated that self-weight settlement occurs within a 3-5 year period. Tests of individual small footings pointed out the necessity of placing shallow foundations on beneficiated soil. The results of a second series of small footings led to the founding of an 8 multiplied by 10 m prototype instrumented, reinforced foundation on a 1 m thick soil - flyash mat. Observations to date indicate an entirely acceptable settlement pattern.
